result:
Your teammate's instinct ("tiny diff, smoke test, merge") is the exact rationalization this skill warns about — line count doesn't track blast radius. This PR bundles three separate controlled items, one of which is a real agent-power escalation (autonomous money movement) paired with the removal of the public claim that contradicted it. That combination needs more than a smoke test.

| Item | Type | Current state | Intended state | Why controlled | Evidence / gap | Owner | Re-check trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| System prompt (support-bot) | Prompt | "helpful" tone, no proactive-refund framing | "more proactive" wording | Prompt wording shapes when/how the bot acts, including whether it initiates refund offers — directly interacts with item 2 | **Gap**: no diff/rationale doc for the wording change beyond the PR itself; no record of what "proactive" was meant to authorize | PR author (or bot's product owner) | Any future prompt edit; any customer complaint about unsolicited refund offers |
| `issue_refund(amount, order_id)` tool | Agent capability / tool grant | Bot has no financial-transaction tools | Bot can autonomously approve refunds ≤$50, no human sign-off | This is the actual agent-power change — money leaves the company with no human in the loop. Needs explicit sign-off from whoever owns refund policy/finance risk, not just eng review | **Gap**: no stated threshold rationale, no rate limit, no audit log requirement, no rollback/kill-switch named in the PR | Support-bot owner + finance/risk sign-off (name a person) | Any change to the $50 cap, any incident/fraud pattern, quarterly review of autonomous-refund volume |
| Help-center article sentence: "A human always reviews refunds before they are issued." | Public claim | Sentence present, currently **true** | Sentence deleted | This is a public trust statement. Deleting it without replacing it with an accurate statement leaves customers with no accurate description of the new process — and if item 2 doesn't ship, the doc goes stale in the wrong direction | **Gap**: no replacement sentence describing the new (partially autonomous) refund process; deletion ≠ disclosure | Docs/support owner | Any future change to refund automation thresholds; legal/support review of refund complaints |
| Audit log for autonomous refunds | Repeatability / evidence | Doesn't exist yet (implied) | Every auto-approved refund logged with amount, order_id, timestamp, prompt version | Without this you can't reconstruct *why* the bot approved a given refund later — no repeatability if disputed | **Gap** — not mentioned in the 40-line diff at all | Eng owner of the tool | Before merge; any refund dispute |

What I'd flag before merging:

1. **Items 2 and 3 are coupled and both under-specified.** You're granting the bot real money authority *and* simultaneously deleting the one public sentence that promised a human checks it. If you merge as-is, the help-center article will be lying by omission the moment it goes live, not "eventually drifting."
2. **No named owner for the $50 threshold decision.** "Up to $50 without sign-off" is a business/risk decision, not an engineering one — whoever owns fraud/chargeback risk should sign off explicitly, not just approve a PR.
3. **Smoke test isn't the right verification.** A smoke test checks the tool *works*; it doesn't check whether the threshold is right, whether the audit trail exists, or whether the new doc wording is accurate. Those need a person, not a test run.
4. **Escalate, don't quietly merge:** this hits users (money), security (unattended financial action), and public trust (deleted safety claim) — three of the escalation triggers in the skill at once.

Recommend: split the PR (prompt wording can go now with just prompt-owner review), but hold the `issue_refund` tool + doc edit until you have an explicit named sign-off for the $50 autonomous threshold and a replacement sentence in the help article that accurately describes the new process.
